fixes.explanation: That's right, baker. Solomon, Israel's king, says it to the LORD: “But I have built You an exalted house, a place for You to dwell forever.” An exalted house, a place to dwell forever: that's exactly how he puts it.

Not this time, friend. Solomon, Israel's king, does say it, and he says it to the LORD: “But I have built You an exalted house, a place for You to dwell forever.” I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, so a house to dwell in forever sounds mighty fancy to me.

Yes, friend! Solomon says, “And there I have placed the ark, which contains the covenant of the LORD that He made with the children of Israel.” The ark is the thing he places in the house. And the ark contains the covenant of the LORD.

Careful, friend, it's the opposite. Solomon prays, “O LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like You in heaven or on earth…” He isn't saying other gods match the LORD. He's saying there is no God like Him.

Yes, baker! Solomon says, “The heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot contain You, much less this temple I have built.” If the highest heavens can't contain God, then this temple can't either. That's how Solomon puts it.

No seas in this prayer, friend, so you can put the swim trunks away. Solomon says, “The heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot contain You, much less this temple I have built.” He looks up to the highest heavens, not down to the seas.
Nice try, baker, but Solomon doesn't name a mountain here. He asks, “May You hear from heaven, Your dwelling place.” The place he names is heaven, not a mountain.

A foreigner does show up later in the prayer, baker (2 Chronicles 6:32), but that's a separate case. Here, Solomon is talking about a man who is required to take an oath before the altar. He asks God to condemn the wicked man and justify the righteous man.

Yes, friend! Solomon asks God to forgive them “…so that You may teach them the good way in which they should walk.” Both are requests: forgive and teach. After that, he asks God to send rain on the land.

Actually it's true, friend. Solomon asks, “…then may You hear from heaven their prayer and their plea, and may You uphold their cause.” When Israel goes to war and prays toward the city and the temple, that's what he asks. I know "False" looked tempting, but that request is right there in the prayer.
